{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABUZiU_A", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzg97SpA", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 13, "title": "Add contribution, review, and scope-control guidelines", "body": "## Goal

Add a small, explicit development workflow for this repository so Issue-driven work stays focused, reviewable, and appropriately scoped.

The repository is being reset to a minimal baseline, so this is a good time to establish the development rules before new implementation work begins.

## Reference

Use the following files from [takahirox/gitweave](https://github.com/takahirox/gitweave) as the primary reference:

- [Issue template](https://github.com/takahirox/gitweave/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md)
- [Pull Request template](https://github.com/takahirox/gitweave/blob/main/.github/pull_request_template.md)
- [Development Flow](https://github.com/takahirox/gitweave/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md)
- [Review Guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/gitweave/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md)

The intent is not to copy every word mechanically, but to adopt the same core development discipline and adapt it to this project.

## Files to add

At minimum:

```text
.github/
  ISSUE_TEMPLATE/
    issue.md
  pull_request_template.md

docs/
  development-flow.md
  review-guidelines.md
```

If a short `CONTRIBUTING.md` is useful as an index to these documents, add it only if it improves discoverability without duplicating the same policy text.

## Issue template

Keep the Issue template intentionally small.

Suggested structure:

```md
## Problem

Describe the problem or need.

## Expected outcome

Describe what should be true when this Issue is complete.

## Context

Add relevant background, constraints, examples, references, or related Issues.
```

The Issue defines the scope of the work. Requirements that are not in the Issue should not be invented during implementation.

## Pull Request template

Suggested structure:

```md
## Summary

Describe what changed.

## Outcome

Describe the resulting behavior, including before/after behavior when useful.

## Validation

Describe how the change was validated.

## Related issues

Link the Issue(s) this PR addresses.

## Scope check

- [ ] This PR fully addresses the Issue it claims to resolve.
- [ ] This PR does not include unrelated work.
- [ ] This PR does not add speculative abstractions, extensibility, frameworks, or subsystems that are not needed by the Issue.
- [ ] If this PR intentionally implements only part of an Issue, that is stated clearly and the Issue is not presented as fully resolved.
- [ ] Validation maps to the Issue's expected outcome / acceptance criteria.
```

The exact wording can be refined, but the scope check should remain concise and meaningful rather than becoming a long ritual checklist.

## Development flow

Document the default flow:

```text
Issue
  ↓
Implementation
  ↓
Pull Request
  ↓
Review
  ↓
Revision if needed
  ↓
Merge
```

Key rules:

1. Work starts from an Issue.
2. The Issue defines the intended problem and expected outcome.
3. If the Issue is ambiguous, clarify it before implementation instead of inventing requirements.
4. A PR should only claim to close an Issue when it fully addresses that Issue.
5. Partial work is allowed when intentional, but it must be labeled as partial and must not close the parent Issue unless the remaining scope has been explicitly split out.
6. Review is required before merge.
7. Merge only after the PR is both correct and appropriately scoped.

## Review guidelines

The central review question should be:

> Does this Pull Request completely address the Issue, without adding changes that are not justified by the Issue?

Review in both directions:

### No missing scope

Do not approve a PR as completing an Issue when required work is still missing.

Watch for:

- incomplete acceptance criteria;
- only one part of a multi-part Issue being implemented;
- missing validation for a required behavior;
- documentation or migration work omitted when explicitly required by the Issue.

### No unnecessary scope

Avoid over-engineering.

Watch for:

- unnecessary abstractions;
- speculative extensibility;
- unrelated refactoring;
- new frameworks or subsystems without a demonstrated need;
- configuration or policy added "for the future";
- solving adjacent problems that were not requested.

Prefer the smallest coherent change that fully solves the Issue.

This is especially important for AI-generated changes, which can easily produce broader or more elaborate implementations than necessary.

### Ordinary quality

Also review:

- correctness;
- clarity;
- consistency with the current architecture;
- appropriate tests / validation;
- documentation updates when behavior changes;
- security/privacy implications where relevant.

## Merge policy

A PR is ready to merge only when:

- it fully satisfies the Issue it claims to resolve;
- it has no unjustified scope or complexity;
- validation is sufficient;
- review feedback has been resolved;
- the PR description accurately reflects what was implemented.

Do not merge a PR simply because CI passes if the implementation is incomplete or over-scoped.

## Language policy

Repository collaboration artifacts should be written in **English**.

This includes, at minimum:

- Issues;
- Pull Request titles and descriptions;
- review comments;
- Issue/PR comments;
- commit messages;
- repository documentation;
- code comments intended as maintained documentation;
- user-facing developer instructions in the repository.

Code identifiers should also use English unless there is a strong domain-specific reason otherwise.

Japanese may still appear where it is part of:

- test fixtures;
- speech-recognition sample data;
- example Japanese transcripts;
- Japanese-language product behavior being tested;
- proper nouns or other content that must remain in Japanese.

The purpose of this rule is to keep development collaboration and project history consistently readable across tools, contributors, and AI agents.

## Avoid duplication

Keep the policy set small.

Do not repeat the same rules across README, templates, CONTRIBUTING, and multiple docs unless there is a clear navigation reason.

Prefer:

- templates for prompting authors;
- `development-flow.md` for workflow;
- `review-guidelines.md` for review criteria;
- a short link/index from README or CONTRIBUTING if needed.

## Compatibility

Backward compatibility with the previous prototype is not required. These workflow documents should describe the new development process only.

## Definition of done

- An Issue template exists and is concise.
- A PR template exists and includes a practical scope check.
- Development flow is documented.
- Review and merge criteria are documented.
- The documents explicitly guard against both under-implementation and over-engineering.
- The documents explicitly state that repository collaboration and documentation are written in English.
- The policy is small enough to be read and followed in practice.
